I tend to start replicating the Unix filesystem hierarchy standard in my home directory.

I make $HOME/bin for random, non-installed binaries, $HOME/opt for non-installed applications, $HOME/tmp for me to stash temporary files. Then, when I have to work on a Windows box, I do the same thing, complete with .bashrc and .ssh after I install Cygwin.

Makes sense. I'd still want to keep $HOME/tmp separate from wherever my applications store their generated temporary files, so I can clear $HOME/tmp without restarting applications (and not have to worry about things in $HOME/tmp being deleted before I upload them or if my PC crashes).

I've never had an application touch $HOME/tmp, and none should, because it's a non-standard location. Anything installed through the package manager uses a system tmp folder and anything else I run makes its own .directory.
